short: The final defeat of the Achaean League by the Roman Republic, resulting in the destruction of Corinth and Roman control of Greece.
full:
In 146 BCE, a brief and ill-fated uprising by the Achaean League against Roman hegemony culminated in the Battle of Corinth. The Roman army, commanded by the consul Lucius Mummius, decisively crushed the poorly organized Greek forces outside the city walls. Following the victory, Mummius ordered the complete destruction of Corinth, long one of the wealthiest and most powerful cities in Greece.

The city's men were slaughtered, the women and children sold into slavery, and its vast treasures were shipped to Rome. The brutal sack of Corinth served as a terrifying example to any who would resist Roman rule, effectively ending Greek political independence and marking the beginning of direct Roman administration over the Greek peninsula.
